title: Which apps alert you when news affects the stocks you own?
summary: Schwab, Fidelity and Seeking Alpha send news alerts on stocks you hold. How they compare with Yahoo, Google, TradingView, Perplexity and Astor.
body_markdown:
## Can your brokerage app alert you about news?


Yes, with limits. Brokerage alerts are built around your positions at that firm.


**Schwab** documents the widest range of the three. Its guide to alerts lists price and volume alerts, dividend alerts, earnings-date and earnings-release alerts, and news alerts based on news stories or press releases for securities on a watchlist or in a portfolio. Alerts go by email or to a wireless device. Schwab also announced Charley, an AI assistant that answers questions about balances and positions, rolling out in phases to eligible US retail clients starting in October 2026.


**Fidelity** says its alerts can notify you about specific stock movements, economic announcements and other news, sent as push notifications in the Fidelity app, and price-trigger alerts can also come by text or email.


**Robinhood** ‘s built-in notifications are mostly about price. You can get alerts when a stock you hold moves 5% or 10%, set custom price or indicator alerts, and get email for significant moves. For news, Robinhood Gold members get Portfolio Digests, AI-generated summaries of the market backdrop, the holdings driving your returns, top movers and upcoming events like earnings. Digests are part of a rolling release and use information from your Robinhood account, excluding IRAs.
